**detailed_description:**

The target video uses a warm, realistic lifestyle vlog style with soft afternoon natural light filtering through large café windows, a gently shallow depth of field, and subtle hand-held camera breathing. The milk tea shop interior features light wooden round tables, pastel pink and cream wall panels, a backlit illuminated menu board on the wall, and faint bokeh of other patrons seated in the background. All character lip movements are driven by `drive_audio` and synchronized with the driving audio syllable by syllable (口型与驱动音频逐音节同步).

[Shot 1] A medium two-shot frames `<Subject 1>` on the left and `<Subject 2>` on the right, seated across from each other at a small round wooden table. `<Subject 2>` holds a clear plastic cup of light-brown milk tea with chewy black boba pearls settled at the bottom, a straw piercing the lid, and raises it halfway to her lips, about to take a sip. `<Subject 1>`, in her champagne satin slip dress and silver heart pendant, turns her head toward `<Subject 2>`, her eyes narrowing playfully and one eyebrow lifting. `<Subject 1>` (S1) speaks in a light, teasing young female voice; her lips part to form each syllable in sync with `drive_audio`, her lower jaw dropping slightly on open vowels and her lips rounding on the final "ao", saying `<d>[中文] 你昨天不是说要减肥吗？</d>`. After the line, her lips close into an amused half-smile and she tilts her chin a fraction.

[Shot 2] At 00:03.500, the shot cuts to a close-up of `<Subject 2>`, the woman in the yellow rose-print dress. She lowers the milk tea cup slightly from her mouth and gives `<Subject 1>` a confident, unapologetic look, her chin lifting a fraction. `<Subject 2>` (S2) responds in a brighter, matter-of-fact young female voice; her mouth opens and closes with each syllable in sync with `drive_audio`, her upper teeth briefly visible as she says "对", her jaw moving naturally through the longer second phrase, saying `<d>[中文] 对啊，所以我把奶茶换成了无糖的。</d>`. She gives a small self-satisfied nod and taps the side of the cup with one fingertip.

[Shot 3] At 00:07.000, the shot cuts to a close-up of `<Subject 1>`, who glances pointedly down at the black boba pearls visible through the clear cup held off-screen, then back up at `<Subject 2>` with a knowing smirk. `<Subject 1>` (S1) asks; her lips purse slightly on the "那" initial and part cleanly with the question's rising intonation, her jaw moving lightly in sync with `drive_audio`, saying `<d>[中文] 那你还加珍珠？</d>`. Her eyebrows rise and she lets a soft breath through her nose.

[Shot 4] At 00:09.000, the shot cuts to a close-up of `<Subject 2>`. She puffs her cheeks almost imperceptibly, then leans forward slightly and taps the boba pearls through the cup wall with a righteous expression. `<Subject 2>` (S2) retorts; her mouth stretches wide on the "嚼" vowel and her jaw drops emphatically on "不算喝", every syllable locked to `drive_audio`, saying `<d>[中文] 珍珠是嚼的，不算喝。</d>`. She seals her lips in a stubborn little pout and lifts the cup as if to defend it.

[Shot 5] At 00:12.000, the shot cuts back to a medium two-shot of both women. `<Subject 1>` bursts out laughing, leaning back slightly and waving one hand dismissively, while `<Subject 2>` takes a quick sip through the straw with a guilty-but-smiling look. `<Subject 1>` (S1) laughs aloud, her mouth wide open in a natural laugh—lips retracted, jaw dropped, the corners of her eyes crinkling—then says through residual chuckles, her lips forming each syllable of `drive_audio`, `<d>[中文] 哈哈，有道理。</d>`. She shakes her head with a grin and raises her own empty cup in a mock toast. The frame holds on both of them smiling at each other.


**overall_soundscape:**

Warm milk tea shop ambient room tone continues throughout: a low hum of refrigerators and air conditioning, faint clinking of cups and spoons from the service counter, soft background chatter of other patrons at a distance, and a brief wet sucking sound of the straw drawing up boba pearls during the close-up of `<Subject 2>`'s drink.

**non_diegetic_music:**

A light, bouncy ukulele-and-whistle background track at a cheerful 110 BPM, entering softly under the first line, maintaining a playful comedic tone, and swelling slightly under the final laugh before fading out by the last frame.

**segment_continuity:**

This video is produced in consecutive segments, but it is ONE continuous performance and one unbroken storyline — the joins must be invisible. Every segment after the first picks up exactly where the previous segment ended and flows naturally and seamlessly into the next part of the plot:

- The opening frame of each following segment reproduces the previous segment's final frame item by item: composition, camera angle and distance, each subject's screen position, posture and body orientation, the exact facial expression (gaze direction, eyebrows, mouth corners, whether the teeth show, how far the mouth is open), the amplitude and direction of every motion in progress, every prop in its place, the background and the light.
- Motion continues, never restarts: the handover frame holds the closing state of the previous segment, and the camera path, the direction and speed of every action and the performance energy of the following segment all develop out of it. Never replay the handover itself, and never re-shoot an action that has already happened.
- The plot continues, never resets: a line, a laugh, a gesture, a glance, a step or a reaction that is in progress at the end of one segment is still in progress at the start of the next, and finishes or settles naturally over the following moments. No segment may open with a re-establishing shot, a recap, a neutral pose, lowered hands or a calmer face; the emotional energy is identical on both sides of the join.
- Framing lock across the join: the opening frame's camera height, scale and composition edges must match the final frame of the reference video exactly. The camera never re-frames, never re-centers, never zooms or settles at a join — the geometry is continuous, as if the whole video were one unbroken shot.
- Background lock: in every segment the background and environment follow the scene reference in <Picture 2> exactly — the same room layout, furniture, props, colors and lighting in every segment. The set is never redesigned, replaced or gradually altered between segments, and the scene reference always overrides any background visible in the handover frame or in a previous segment.
- Color lock: <Video 1> has exactly one fixed job in this video: it is the color reference, and nothing else. It is a frame from the middle of the first segment, blurred beyond recognition, and it exists only to be taken colors from — in every segment the palette, white balance, saturation, exposure and skin tones follow <Video 1> exactly, and the picture never drifts warmer, cooler, brighter or duller as the segments progress. No person, scene, pose, composition or motion is ever taken from <Video 1>: who everyone is, where they stand and what happens come only from the reference pictures, the handover frame and the script — <Video 1> decides colors, and only colors. The blurred handover frame <Picture 3> is a placement guide only: it fixes positions, poses and composition, and its colors are never followed — whenever its colors disagree with <Video 1>, <Video 1> wins.
- Open on a held beat: each following segment first holds the previous segment's ending pose and mood for a short beat (about 1 second) — the hold is a still tableau: pose, positions, framing and composition stay exactly unchanged, the bodies essentially still like a still image, with only the faintest signs of life — a breath, a blink, light and air moving — and only then does the next beat of the plot begin. This held moment is never a hard freeze of duplicated frames and never a new establishing shot.
- Constant rendering, no escalation: the rendering style, the surface textures, and the intensity of expressions and gestures remain exactly as in the reference images in every segment — never more stylized, more exaggerated or more dramatic than the segment before. Consistency beats expressiveness at every join.
- The drive audio alone decides when each line begins and ends; the lip performance follows it across the join with no pause, no repeated syllable and no dropped word.
